messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Large .Rdata files
parts:
Hi,
I have had the experience several times where my R session -- where I am
doing nothing but aroma.affymetrix commands -- starts to have a large
.Rdata file (e.g. 50,000KB or larger). I can't figure out why this would
happen, since nothing I am doing with aroma.affymetrix creates large R
objects (or so I thought). It slows everything down, and also sometimes
gives me memory problems in allocating vectors when I'm running a
calculation like 'fit'. I have looked at my objects in my global
environment using 'object.size' (I know, not really the size, but better
than nothing), but nothing seems very large in comparison with anything
else.

e.g.
>
sort(sapply(ls(all.names=T),function(x){object.size(get(x))}))

...etc
hbLite
56544
.__M__MAplot:affy
115864
indices
119016

Short of erasing everything (which is what I did last time) is there
some way I can diagnose this and get rid of whatever is large? Or is it
that R storing something and not letting go? (I'm on Windows, by the way)

I'm not exactly sure when my .Rdata file gets so large, but a couple of
times I was running something overnight and came back to find out there
was an error (usually stemming from the problem of old out-of date runs
needing to be wiped out more completely, or I wiped them out but then
didn't retrace enough steps). Could something be 'left' in R and not
getting removed when there was a problem? I'm totally clueless about how
R actually uses memory, so it's difficult for me to even make
intelligent guesses.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

> was an error (usually stemming from the problem of old out-of date runs

> getting removed when there was a problem? I'm totally clueless about how
> R actually uses memory, so it's difficult for me to even make
> intelligent guesses.

Have you tried to call gc() before exiting (and saving the .RData
file) and what do it report?

The package caches some results that takes a long time to
calculate/extract on file, but in some cases also in memory,
especially CDF data. Do you have any aroma.affymetrix object around?
If you do, object.size() will *not* give you their true sizes, but
objectSize() will (that function is defined in R.oo an operates on all
objects of class Object). See if you can find an object that is
large. If you have an AffymetrixCelSet object, say 'cs', but not an
AffymetrixCdfFile object, try also to do:

cdf <- getCdf(cs)
objectSize(cdf)

If you find a large object, call gc() on it, e.g. gc(cdf). That will
remove cached data (which are redundant) from memory.

It might also have to with so called "promises", which has nothing to
do aroma.affymetrix per se. That is more complicated, but I also know
they've added methods for cleaning out such before saving to file.

Personally I never save .RData files because I feel much more
comfortable starting a clean/fresh R session and use an R script to
set up all variables. Since aroma.affymetrix detects if things have
already been calculated, the overhead is not that big. (So, this is
also a reason why I don't experience the problems you have, in case it
is due to aroma.affymetrix).

Cheers

Henrik

Hi Karen,

I just got a largish .Rdata file after only working with
affymetrix.aroma objects/commands for awhile and managed to fix it
following Henrik's suggestions, so I thought I'd let you know (I guess
I'll post this on the group discussion as well). I wrote a function that
will give the space different objects take up (if they are
affymetrix.aroma objects you have to use a different command, but the
command doesn't work for regular R objects, so it switches back and
forth -- I'm not making promises that they are the same kind of
measurements, etc., but it's at least something) and returns the sizes
and names, sorted by size. So if you look at the output, I see that I
have two large objects, cellInd and csN.

> allObjectSize()
...
calculateResiduals.ExonEffectRmaPlm
fit.ExonEffectRmaPlm

59268 67316

wsNoExon ws

84396 86212

diffrs ratiors

100480 100480

rs1_10 rsExon1_10

102000 102000

rs csN

154508 53451660
cellInd
60938640

cellInd is my own creation and I don't want to delete it because it took
a while to make. But csN is just the reference to the saved normalized
data and shouldn't take up so much space; it's probably the caching that
did it. So then I did a clean up of that object specifically (just
'gc()' didn't do it -- not sure why) and it shrunk down to irrelevant size.

> gc(csN)
> allObjectsSize()
...
csN
plotDataUnit.FirmaModel

31652 32964
cs
getFitFunction.ExonEffectRmaPlm

34540 36612

rsExon rsNoExon
...

ratiors rs1_10

100480 102000

rsExon1_10 rs

102000 154508
cellInd
60938640

My .Rdata file went from around 18,000Kb back to 5,000Kb (I did
save.image() after I cleaned up so I could see the effect, otherwise you
won't see a difference until you do; but you can do this before you save
so that you don't get the freeze while R tries to save the gigantic
files you were saying you saw). I have also gotten much larger .Rdata
files in the past (not as big as yours!), but 18,000Kb was still a large
jump from what it had been when I started R up.

Best,
Elizabeth

Here's my function:
allObjectSize<-function(x=ls(globalenv())){
size<-sapply(x,function(y){
if(inherits(get(y),"Object")) out<-objectSize(get(y))
else out<-object.size(get(y))
return(out)
})
return(sort(size))

}

I've added method gc() to instances of class Object (which all
aroma.affymetrix class inherits from) so when called like you do, e.g.
gc(csN), it will clear all cached fields of object 'csN' and the call
the global gc(). You'll see this if you do:

> print(gc.Object)

function (this, ...)
{
clearCache(this)
gc()
}

On the other hand, the global gc() [now renamed to gc.default()] is
defined in the base package and does exactly what it used to do;
garbage collect R's internal memory. It does *not* recursively call
gc() on Object:s, because first there is no way to add so called hooks
for this, but also because it would be too expensive to do this each
time the garbage collector is in action. Also, cached values in
Object:s are not memory garbage in the common sense; we cache values
for a purpose and might want to reuse them, i.e. they should be
removed only when we explicitly say so. On the other hand, regular
memory garbage are objects lost for ever that we never can reuse. It
might be that another name than gc() for Object:s would be more
appropriate; I just though it was a short convenient name and related
to gc(). As seen above, you can perfectly well just do:

clearCache(csN)

which maybe makes more sense.

If you are interested in exactly what makes an Object large, you can
use the ll() (two L:s) function. Since cached fields are "private"
(prefixed with a dot), you have to do:

ll(csN, private=TRUE)

You'll find that AffymetrixCelSet:s (which I just guess 'csN' is)
caches a few different kind of values.

> > gc(csN)
> > allObjectsSize()
> ...
> csN
> plotDataUnit.FirmaModel

> cs

> won't see a difference until you do; but you can do this before you save
> so that you don't get the freeze while R tries to save the gigantic
> files you were saying you saw). I have also gotten much larger .Rdata
> files in the past (not as big as yours!), but 18,000Kb was still a large
> jump from what it had been when I started R up.

I'll admit that I'm a rookie when it comes to .RData files, but is
18MB considered large?!? If it is, it must have been the case that
you could never save the image for BioC sessions, because there you
would have had objects of size 100-1000MBs.

Looking at the help pages, save.image() saves the image compressed by
default. This slows down things quite a bit, e.g.

% R --vanilla
> x <- 1:3e7; object.size(x); gc()
[1] 120000024
used (Mb) gc trigger (Mb) max used (Mb)
Ncells 234329 6.3 467875 12.5 407500 10.9
Vcells 15103885 115.3 22501932 171.7 20103882 153.4
> t1a <- system.time({save.image(compress=TRUE)})
> s1 <- file.info(".RData")$size
> t1b <- system.time({load(".RData")})
> gc()
used (Mb) gc trigger (Mb) max used (Mb)
Ncells 234919 6.3 467875 12.5 407500 10.9
Vcells 15104002 115.3 31854461 243.1 30104134 229.7
> t2a <- system.time({save.image(compress=FALSE)})
> s2 <- file.info(".RData")$size
> t2b <- system.time({load(".RData")})
# File size
> s1/s2
[1] 0.5018958
# Saving time (4-5 times!)
> t1a/t2a
[1] 9.4039634 0.4583333 4.7396947 NA NA
# Loading time
> t1b/t2b
[1] 1.177966 1.375000 1.173130 NA NA

See ?save.image on how to use the 'save.image.defaults' option to
change the default value on 'compress' to FALSE.

Cheers

Henrik

installed when you install the next version of aroma.affymetrix, I've
added objectSize() for regular objects too and the ll() command will
report that instead of object.size(), e.g.

> obj <- Object()
> obj$x <- 1:1e6
> ll()
member data.class dimension objectSize
1 author character 1 120
2 obj Object 1 4000024

which give what your allObjectSize() do.

/H

Hi Henrik,
Just a FYI on the .Rdata files because I missed your question in the
midst of your email. 18MB isn't large as a .Rdata file if I'd actually
been creating objects to store in R's memory. It was just that it was a
large and noticable jump from where I had started (5MB) since I hadn't
actually created any new R objects -- so it was a good test case to try
out how to getting rid of the cached objects would effect my saved image
file (Before I could get around a hundred MB as a .Rdata file, so it
would take a bit of time to save and therefore also to test what effect
gc had; it was easier to just delete everything)
Elizabeth

> I've added method gc() to instances of class Object (which all
> aroma.affymetrix class inherits from) so when called like you do, e.g.
> gc(csN), it will clear all cached fields of object 'csN' and the call
> the global gc(). You'll see this if you do:
>
>
>> print(gc.Object)
>>
>
> function (this, ...)
> {
> clearCache(this)
> gc()
> }
>
> On the other hand, the global gc() [now renamed to gc.default()] is
> defined in the base package and does exactly what it used to do;
> garbage collect R's internal memory. It does *not* recursively call
> gc() on Object:s, because first there is no way to add so called hooks
> for this, but also because it would be too expensive to do this each
> time the garbage collector is in action. Also, cached values in
> Object:s are not memory garbage in the common sense; we cache values
> for a purpose and might want to reuse them, i.e. they should be
> removed only when we explicitly say so. On the other hand, regular
> memory garbage are objects lost for ever that we never can reuse. It
> might be that another name than gc() for Object:s would be more
> appropriate; I just though it was a short convenient name and related
> to gc(). As seen above, you can perfectly well just do:
>
> clearCache(csN)
>
> which maybe makes more sense.
>
> If you are interested in exactly what makes an Object large, you can
> use the ll() (two L:s) function. Since cached fields are "private"
> (prefixed with a dot), you have to do:
>
> ll(csN, private=TRUE)
>
> You'll find that AffymetrixCelSet:s (which I just guess 'csN' is)
> caches a few different kind of values.
